scope: One explicit batch of project-generated Rust code-generation object leaves; no product or Agent acceptance claim.

roles.rootPublicationReview: Root read full helper, qualified all selected objects and reviewed actual completion/post-verification; metadata-only publication with explicit limits.

capacity.interpretation: Selection allocation and endpoint available-space change are separate observations. The delta is not a uniquely attributable physical-reclaim measurement or an additive guarantee; later compilation can regenerate these objects.

guards: Fixed hashed manifest and eight hashed fragments; exact names only, no prefix/glob deletion.
No-follow exact directory/leaf access, regular object/header/owner/metadata checks and closed hardlink groups validated before deletion.
Fresh compiler/linker/test process checks and one exact-directory open-file inventory; selected open references refuse.
Per-name identity and expected decreasing link-count rechecks, followed by held-object link-count verification and final selected-name absence.
Single-use private output, natural exit and partial-failure preservation; no automatic retry.

retained.rmetaRlibBuildFingerprintAndOtherNonsele: All nonselected direct dependency entries, including rmeta/rlib, matched the recorded metadata. build/.fingerprint and all other directories were outside deletion targets, not full-content-fingerprinted.

limits: Sequential stat/open/unlink is not globally atomic and does not lock out future namespace writers. Process/open-file observations are point-in-time guards.
The helper journal is not a power-loss transaction or resumable cleanup mechanism.
No test, build, App/Agent operation or installed acceptance was performed by this cleanup.
The summary drafter also authored the helper; Root operated and verified deletion, acceptance_index independently read the actual journal and current retained/absent filesystem state.
privacy: Only qualification/helper/result/post-verification metadata references and hashes are included. Raw per-object JSONL, process/open-file output, retained-entry maps, private payloads and user-data fingerprints are excluded.
